study type: Mixed-methods study employing semi-structured interviews within the context of an existing longitudinal cohort study.
outcome: Parent experience of caring for an infant with neonatal encephalopathy
Entangled infant and broader family interests
Parents evolving into and finding meaning in their role as an advocate
cohort: Parents of infants diagnosed with neonatal encephalopathy, whose infants were previously enrolled in a longitudinal cohort study of therapeutic hypothermia between 2011 and 2014.
finding: Parents caring for an infant with neonatal encephalopathy experience cumulative loss and grief, entangled infant and broader family interests, and evolve into advocates, finding meaning in this role.
